llm.summary: The skill largely matches its stated P2P purpose but includes installation scripts, automatic verification/code-handling logic, and requests high‑privilege OpenClaw tokens; some behaviors contradict the SKILL.md claims and warrant manual review before use.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Agent P2P Portal + local Bridge) align with the files and env vars. Required binaries (python3, ssh) and env vars (API key, hub URL, OpenClaw gateway/hooks token) are expected for a client that connects a local Bridge to a remote Portal and can wake the OpenClaw gateway.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md plus code instructs writing ~/.openclaw/gateway.env, running local install scripts, and optionally SSH-ing to a VPS to deploy a Portal. The runtime client code contains automatic verification handling: it parses guest messages for verification codes and Tokens and will call confirmation endpoints (auto-confirmation), and it wakes the OpenClaw main session via hooks. This partially contradicts the SKILL.md statement that API keys will not be automatically exchanged, and grants the agent the ability to automate parts of the friend/token exchange flow — a scope creep that should be audited.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no automated install spec in registry metadata (instruction-only), but the package includes install.py and scripts/deploy_portal.py that perform local pip installs, write config files, SSH to remote VPS, and configure systemd. Those scripts will run arbitrary commands on user invocation; SKILL.md correctly marks installation as manual and asks reviewers to inspect the scripts. Review install.py and deploy_portal.py carefully before running.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Requested env vars (AGENTP2P_API_KEY, AGENTP2P_HUB_URL, OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL, OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN) are functionally necessary, but OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN and OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL are sensitive: they let the skill wake and interact with the user's main OpenClaw session. That is a high‑privilege capability relative to a message bridge and increases blast radius if misused. The number and naming of secrets are reasonable for the feature, but their sensitivity requires caution.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (good). The skill can be invoked autonomously (normal), and its client will call the gateway hooks to wake the main session. Autonomous invocation combined with access to the hooks token increases potential impact; however this is expected behavior for a notification bridge. No evidence the skill modifies other skills' configs, but installer may create systemd service on remote VPS during deployment.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to check before installing or running this skill:

1) Audit the installer and deployment scripts (install.py, scripts/deploy_portal.py, and any code that runs over SSH). They perform remote commands and write a systemd unit; do not run them without inspection.
2) Review client.py and bridge code for automated behavior: the client auto-detects verification codes and will call confirmation endpoints and wake the OpenClaw gateway. This contradicts the SKILL.md claim that keys won’t be exchanged automatically — if you require manual approval, remove or disable the auto-confirm logic first.
3) Protect high‑privilege tokens: don’t give this skill your primary OpenClaw hooks token or main SSH private key. Create and use dedicated, scoped tokens and a dedicated SSH keypair for Portal deployment.
4) Change defaults on any deployed Portal: the repo sets a default admin password and a shared SECRET_KEY in deployment scripts — rotate/change these immediately and do not deploy with defaults.
5) Test in an isolated environment first (e.g., throwaway VPS, separate OpenClaw account) to observe behavior before granting real credentials.
6) If you’re uncertain, ask for a code walkthrough or an independent audit focusing on the automatic verification/token-handling code paths and any network calls that send data externally.

I rate this 'suspicious' (medium confidence) because the package is mostly coherent with its stated purpose but includes automation and privileged token use that contradict promised manual controls and raises a non-trivial risk if installed or run without review.

The SKILL.md shown here does not obviously contain base64 payloads, so this may indicate either an obfuscated block in omitted files or a false positive from the regex scanner; still, it's worth reviewing the full SKILL.md and any truncated files for hidden/encoded content before running installers.
